Kṛtyakalpataru
dh. by Lakṣmīdhara, mahāsāndhivigrahika an. dharmādhikārin of King Govindacandra of Kanauj (1104-54 A. D.); son of Bhaṭṭa Hṛdayadhara who also held the same office in that court. In 14 Kāṇḍas: Brahmacāriº, Gṛhasthaº, Naiyatakālaº (Āhnika), Śrāddhaº, Dānaº, Pratiṣṭhāº, Pūjāº, Tīrthaº, Vrataº, Śuddhiº, Rājadharmaº, Vyavahāraº, Śāntiº an. Mokṣaº.
Drawn upon heavily by later compilers of digests; the earliest to quote him is Aniruddha of Bengal (C. 1160 A. D.).
On the mutual chronological relation of Lakṣmīdhara, Vijñāneśvara an. Aparārka see Kane, HDS. I. [Page274-a. p.. 317-8; K. V. R. Aiyangar, Kṛ. kalpa (Dāna). GOS. XCII. p.. 21 ff.
